feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Evidence from iteration 1: the ±0.03 m span lifted the s-bend from 5/20 to 16/20 finishes, but the slalom stayed at 0/20 with mean line_loss_events 1.05 and max_error 0.064, so the outer sensors still lose the line before the exit. The s-bend steering_oscillation rose from 0.25 to 0.34 when the span widened, so jitter is now a possible side effect of wider reach. Iteration 0 showed the oval is not limited by the drivetrain (1.84 s, far under 3 s). For this candidate, the Integrator keeps kp 3.0 and kd 0.75 unchanged, so the next race isolates the footprint. Next-race decisions: if the slalom still shows line loss before exit (line_loss_events of about 1 or more and max_error near 0.06), the coverage change is not enough, so reduce sensor y from 0.06 to 0.04 m to cut the lead. If s-bend steering_oscillation stays above about 0.3 while finishes rise, the wider footprint is causing jitter, so return sensor_size to 0.012 and try a narrower span of ±0.025 m with 0.0083 m pitch. If line loss on the slalom falls but finishes remain zero, look at wheel_track as turn authority.
requested_changes: If the slalom still shows line loss before exit (iteration-1 baseline: 1.05 events, max_error 0.064), keep the 16 mm footprint and reduce the sensor lead from y = 0.06 to y = 0.04 m for all seven sensors, since lag was not evident (slalom steering_oscillation 0.198).

If the s-bend steering_oscillation stays above about 0.3 (iteration 1 measured 0.34 versus 0.25 in iteration 0) while finishes rise, return sensor_size to 0.012 m and keep the ±0.03 m span, testing whether the larger footprint is what adds jitter.

If line-loss events on the slalom fall but no trial finishes, reduce wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 m to increase turn authority at the slalom's direction changes. The oval's 1.84 s finish shows the drivetrain has time margin for this.
